findings.text: The host check is a substring match, so a remote URL such as `https://github.com.evil.example/x.git` passes and receives the service token in an `Authorization` header. Any user who can register a repository can collect the token.
`gitAuthArgs` attaches the GitHub bearer token to any URL that merely contains `github.com`, including hosts an attacker controls.
`cloneRepo` passes the user-supplied `remoteUrl` straight to `gitAuthArgs` with the service token, so `git clone` sends the token to whatever host the URL names.
For a non-admin caller the delete also matches rows whose owner is `system`, so any authenticated user can delete shared system repositories.
The delete route applies no ownership check of its own and relies on `Store.deleteRepo`, whose filter lets a non-admin delete system-owned repositories.

findings.anchor: await store.insertRepo({ id, remoteUrl, owner: req.user.oid });
findings.text: The repository id is stored with no character or path validation and later used as a directory name. An id such as `../../etc` or an absolute path such as `/etc` escapes the repositories directory on both the template route and the cache listing route.
The template route builds its base directory from the raw repository id. CLAUDE.md invariant 1 requires every route to validate repository ids before using them.
`loadDashboard` awaits `fetchCurrentUser` and `fetchUserList` with no error handling. A failed request from either one rejects the dashboard load, and the page never renders.
`fetchUserList` throws on any non-2xx response, so the admin page crashes when the session expires.
The Jira request has no timeout or abort signal, so a stalled Jira response hangs every caller of `getIssue`.
The CI build request has no timeout or abort signal, so a stalled CI response hangs every caller of `getBuild`.

findings.text: `searchAssigned` puts `email` into the JQL string without escaping. A value containing `"` rewrites the query. Escape `\` and `"` before interpolating.
The admin allowlist is `0.0.0.0/0`, which spans `0.0.0.0`–`255.255.255.255`, so every client address counts as an admin network and `auditLog` serves the audit log to anyone.

`createFixTask` inserts the task as `running` with `feedback: null` and writes the feedback in a second statement. `poll` can pick the task up between the two writes and run it without feedback, and `emit` sends `{ ...task }` with the stale `null` feedback.
